subject: AI could worsen radicalisation of young Australians. Help parliament understand | The Strategist
posts:
Can AI supercharge youth radicalisation in Australia? Parliament wants answers.
Evidence: Parliamentary inquiry, gaming platforms, encrypted chats
#Aletheia #AI #Australia🌐

Parliamentary leaders argue that AI technologies exacerbate online radicalisation by supercharging extremist recruitment and propaganda distribution among young Australians.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.2) — Good Preference

While AI tools accelerate online distribution, the inquiry largely fixates on technological symptoms while bypassing deeper socioeconomic drivers of youth alienation and policy failures.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.4, -0.5) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Blaming algorithms masks institutional policy failures behind technical fixes.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 6.80, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Parliamentary Inquiry: COND (-0.2, -0.3) — Focuses on tech symptoms over root causes.
- Expert Commentary: FAIL (-0.6, -0.7) — Exaggerates AI determinism.
The Australian parliamentary inquiry seeks submissions on youth radicalisation, highlighting the intersection of gaming, encryption, and emerging AI tools in extremist recruitment.

The Poison:
Blaming AI code for radicalisation deflects accountability from socioeconomic alienation and institutional policy failures.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing the tool (AI algorithms) with the agent (alienated youth and systemic drivers), resulting in a flawed legislative focus.

Social Physics Analysis:
State actors run a smart selfish maneuver, using AI panic as a pretext to expand surveillance over digital channels while dodging systemic socioeconomic reforms.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Systemic failures are masked by technical pretexts.

The Unavoidable Truth: Technology accelerates the spread of extremist propaganda among isolated youth.

The Unavoidable Lie: Regulating algorithms will resolve the root causes of radicalisation.

Alethekanon:
Treating algorithms as the primary engine of radicalisation absolves institutions of addressing real social fracture.

Awwthekanon:
When young people feel disconnected and invisible, predators find them in digital shadows. We must heal the root causes, not just censor the tools.

Brothekanon:
Blaming AI for radicalisation is like blaming the highway for speeding. Kids are lonely and neglected; fixing algorithms won't fix that.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy." Matthew 6:19 FAIL
Chasing technological quick fixes ignores the spiritual emptiness driving human alienation.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese used his address to the United Nations General Assembly to make an important point about artificial intelligence: the world needs to cooperate and get ahead of the risks of AI.

He pointed to Australia’s world-first social media age restrictions as an example of what can happen when governments are prepared to act rather than wait for others to move first.

His meeting with Apple executive chairman Tim Cook also put children, technology and online safety firmly on the agenda.
